description: Reviewed target-fit exclusions for the UK terminal battery (schema 2 per #610). Each entry defers one calibration target whose |relative error| breaches the 25% release bound, with the defect diagnosed, tracked, and owned elsewhere; the receipt records the reasoning, approver, adjudication reference, approval date, and expiry. The gate keeps the target BOUND in calibration (exclusion applies to the release fence only, never the solve), reports dormant entries, FAILS stale ones (targets back inside the bound), and FAILS expired ones until the adjudication is renewed, so this register cannot rot.

dwp.uc.households_single_with_children@2.reason: UC with-children support residual, not a fit defect: initial eligible support runs 4.24m benunits vs 6.76m DWP admin after the #750 pension-wealth split, the #813 re-bind proved this cell's grain honest (family-type cells partition dwp.uc.households exactly), and the 0.55/0.70/0.85 take-up probes proved marginal claimants ~10:1 childless, so no calibration-side lever reaches it. Root cause evidenced by the donor-truth benchmark on #809: the wealth re-draw over-spreads countable capital >16k to a 38.3% household share vs the WAS donor's 28.6%, suppressing eligibility; the fix is the #145 draw-quality workstream. Deferred one month to unblock the first certified cut. Historical-basis annotation (2026-09-07, PR #879): The preceding text preserves the original adjudication rationale as historical evidence. The FRS claimant/partner correction changes membership of the single-with-children cell, so the #813 support, take-up and wealth-draw attribution above has not been revalidated under the corrected measurement. Fresh adjudication is required; this annotation is not a renewal or new approval and changes no exclusion decision, approver, approval/expiry date or gate threshold. Source-role/codebook, redraw and native-entitlement work remain separate from calibration relabelling. See https://github.com/PolicyEngine/microcosm/blob/7fd55db0a548c0b74566d56fdec776a97e84b89b/experiments/879-corrected-calibration-comparison.md#historical-uc-fit-deferral-rationales.

obr.capital_gains_tax@2025.reason: Vintage conflict, not a fit defect: the Chronicle re-pin (microcosm#874) put HMRC's 2024-25 CGT outturn on the feed (£127.3bn of chargeable gains, 584k taxpayers, against £69.9bn / 403k in 2023-24 — the forestalling year ahead of the 30 October 2024 rate rise) and the doctrine binds it at face value at the 2025 period; the frame fits both HMRC rows within 0.3% and 2025-26 rates on those gains give £31.4bn of liability (24.7% effective) against OBR's £21.8bn FY2025-26 receipts and HMRC's realised 19.0% on the same gains (+44.2% at the composed calibration; −25% with the 2023-24 gains). The facts stay bound as published; the deliverable is a declared 2024-25 → 2025 translation of the gains total under the WS-C reconciliation layer (#875: the index ruling, applying uprating_index in the compile step, the taxpayer count flat at 584k, the cash-lag mapping for self-assessed OBR lines). While in force the calibrated 2025-26 base carries ~40% more CGT liability than OBR expects.
